citation.title: Opening the Black Box: Low-Dimensional Dynamics in High-Dimensional Recurrent Neural Networks
citation.doi_or_arxiv: unknown (not printed in the extracted text; the article ID neco_a_00409 appears only in a download footer)

topic: Interpretability of trained RNNs. The method finds fixed and slow points by minimizing q=|F(x)|^2/2 and then linearizes the dynamics around those points.
own_question: How do trained RNNs implement their tasks? Studied on a 3-bit flip-flop, a sine-wave generator and a 2-point moving average.
actual_method_and_evidence: The authors run optimization from initial conditions sampled along network trajectories, then do Jacobian eigenanalysis at the points found. The evidence is entirely toy-task and simulation based. It contains no plasma, CES, BES/ECEI or nowcasting content.

claim_checks.allowed_intro_or_theory_claim: For RNN dynamics, minimizing the squared speed can locate fixed and slow points, and linearizing around them can help interpret trained networks.
claim_checks.qualification: Demonstrated only on simple synthetic tasks. Use this only if our paper analyzes the dynamics of a recurrent estimator; we did not implement this method.

validation_if_relevant: Simulated task error only. There is no held-out real-data validation.
forbidden_inferences: That our estimator is interpretable or has a low-dimensional mechanism.
Any physical mechanism in the plasma.
Any support for CES nowcasting, real-time feasibility or causal validity.
Any generalization to recurrent models broadly.
reason_to_include_or_exclude: Exclude unless the paper actually adds a fixed-point or dynamics analysis of a recurrent nowcaster. It is unrelated to the targets, inputs and baselines.
source_scope_note: All extracted page texts supplied; figure/equation visual validation remains separate
